about: Proper names, and the spellings the witnesses write them with.
These manuscripts render New Testament names as Greek transliterations
where other witnesses write the Hebrew: Cochin's יאהנניס is Sloane's
יוחנן. Nothing computes that relation. It is four edits over a
seven-letter word, it carries no Strong's number, and the two share no
consonantal skeleton -- so no measure of similarity will ever reach it,
however it is tuned. Someone who knows has to say so, and this is where.
forms:  every spelling met in a manuscript. Compared on the consonantal
skeleton with final letters folded, so pointing and word-final
forms need not agree with what is written here.
prefer: the form Milah offers the editor. Written POINTED; it is stripped
automatically for an unpointed edition, and points cannot be
invented the other way. It is a member of its own group, so a
witness reading it needs no separate entry in forms.
id:     stable and not shown to anyone. It is what a test asserts on, and
what catches John being filed under Jesus -- a test that a
spelling merely resolves would pass with the groups swapped.
One or two agglutinated prefix letters (ובכלמהש) are peeled, so ולעפהיזוס
reaches עפהיזוס and לסמירנון reaches סמירנון. Shortest peel first, which
is why ולאדיצאן resolves as ו + לאדיצאן and not as ול + אדיצאן: Laodicea
begins with a lamed of its own.
The אל-prefixed forms (אלסמרנה, אלתיאטירה, אלפילדלפיאה) are no longer
reached from this corpus: Sloane writes וְאֶל-סְמֻרְנָה with a hyphen, and
the parser now divides at a hyphen or maqaf, so the bare name is what
arrives here. They are kept as insurance for a witness that glues the
particle on with nothing between -- אל is not a peelable prefix letter,
being 'god', 'to', 'not' and 'these' by turns.
UNCONFIRMED PREFERRED SPELLINGS. Entries marked "unconfirmed": true carry
a preferred form proposed by the transcriber of this file, not settled by
the editor. They go into the edition when accepted, so read them before
trusting them. יוֹחָנָן and יֵשׁוּעַ are not marked: those are settled.
The field is documentation -- Milah does not read it.
This table is meant to stay SMALL. A group outranks a shared Strong's
number in the alignment, so a wrong equivalence beats the dictionary
silently. See the note on kScoreName in app/src/core/align_score.h.
Names can also be kept in hebrew_names.json under the application data
directory. A group there whose id matches one here REPLACES it whole,
spellings included, so a wrong form can be taken out and not merely
added to.

names.note: John. Cochin writes the Greek Iōannēs three ways, metathesising the alef and he; Sloane writes the Hebrew name. Sloane's אנייוחנן at Rev 1:9 is 'I John' run together and is a tokenisation problem, not a spelling of the name.

The truncated ישו is a derogatory shortening; the name is written in full as Yeshua. Cochin abbreviates to יש֞ו, Sloane writes יהושע. Beware: יהושע is also the biblical Joshua, so this group is right for Revelation and would be wrong for a book quoting Joshua son of Nun.
Ephesus, the first of the seven churches. Cochin opens it with ayin, Sloane with alef.

Smyrna. Cochin writes it with a samekh at Rev 1:11 and a zayin at Rev 2:8. אלסמרנה is kept only for a witness that glues the preposition on with nothing between; Sloane's own וְאֶל-סְמֻרְנָה is divided at the hyphen.
Pergamum. Cochin ends it with samekh at Rev 1:11 and mem at Rev 2:12 — a different letter, not a final form, so both are listed.
Thyatira. Cochin opens it with tet, Sloane with tav.
Sardis. Cochin opens it with zayin, Sloane with samekh.
Philadelphia. אלפילדלפיאה is kept for the same glued אל as Smyrna, and for the same reason is not what this corpus actually reaches.
Laodicea. The one that proves the peeling order: Cochin's ולאדיצאן must come off as ו + לאדיצאן, because the name itself begins with a lamed, while Sloane's לאודיקיאה must resolve whole.
